transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I can’t keep my work straight anymore. I work with laundry and dry cleaning, and there are all these tickets and receipts and notes from the workshop, and customer jobs, and somehow they all end up in piles together. Then I’m standing there looking at it like, “Okay, what am I supposed to do first?”  

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I used to be able to sort of manage it, or at least fake my way through with little piles, but now the piles have piles. And then a customer comes in asking about something, and I’m shuffling through papers like I know where it is, but I don’t. I mean, I bought these colored folders once—my sister said color-coding changed her life, but she’s always been like that, very neat, even her junk drawer is neat—anyway, it didn’t really stick for me. So… yeah, that’s what brought me in.
Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with staying organized or focused when you were a kid or teenager, or is this something that's really only become a problem more recently?

Oh no, it goes way back. My mother used to get those teacher comments, like, “She’s bright, but she’s scattered,” which is funny because she kept every report card in this little box with old birthday cards and, I don’t know, insurance papers or something.

But yeah, even in grade school I was losing papers, forgetting to turn things in, needing the teacher to remind me to finish my work. And I talked out of turn a lot, apparently. I remember my mom getting that look when the teacher would say it, like she’d heard it before. So it’s not brand new, it’s just gotten harder to cover up, I guess.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself impulsively interrupting others or blurting things out in daily life now?

Yeah, I do that more than I’d like to admit. I’ll jump into my staff’s conversations before I even think, or I’ll reach right over and “fix” how they’re sorting clothes when nobody asked me to. And then I can see on their faces that it feels like I’m butting in.

It’s not like I’m trying to be rude. I just notice something and my hand or my mouth is already moving. Then afterward I think, why didn’t I just wait?
Can you recall specific examples of this restlessness, impulsivity, or disorganization causing problems before you turned 12 years old?

Yeah, I mean, grade school is where I remember it starting. The teachers would tell my mother I was “bright but scattered”—that exact kind of thing. I was always losing papers, or I’d have the homework done but it would be in the wrong folder or shoved in my desk somewhere.

And talking out of turn, that came up a lot. I’d just say the answer or start talking before I was supposed to. My mother used to sigh when she’d hear it, like, here we go again. I also needed reminders to actually finish my work, not because I couldn’t do it, but because I’d sort of drift off or get caught up in something else. My desk was a disaster too—well, I don’t know if that matters, but it was.
Do you notice these same problems with disorganization, impulsivity, or restlessness affecting you outside of work too—like at home or in your personal relationships?

Yes, it’s not just work. I mean, work is where it shows the loudest because there are tickets and orders and customers standing there, and if I mix up billing or something’s late, everyone knows right away.

But outside of work too, yes. At church I used to help lead some of the planning things—like events, little sign-up sheets, who’s bringing what—and I’ve stepped back from that because people were getting frustrated with me. I’d lose track of what had been decided or jump in and change things, and then it got tense. I hated that, because church is supposed to be where you feel useful, not like you’re making extra work for everyone.

And at the shop, it’s been late orders, confused billing, tense moments with staff and customers… so, yes, it follows me around more than I’d like.
